argument: Temporal locality reuses recently accessed data; spatial locality accesses nearby data. Memory hierarchies exploit both, and performance degrades when the active working set exceeds a cache or memory tier.
boundary: Irregular graph, sparse, and streaming workloads may have weak locality.
Prefetching and reordering can change locality.
Distributed locality includes network topology and data placement.

interpretation: Algorithmic complexity alone can miss dominant movement costs. Efficiency claims should record bytes moved and locality assumptions.
